plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives in cool autumn temperatures and is triggered to flower by shortening day length.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and in Japan the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and honored at the Festival of Happiness.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like pink-lilac flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The strap-shaped leaves appear in spring and die back by summer.
plants.location: Damp meadows and woodland edges of Europe, from the UK to central Europe; widely grown in gardens
plants.funFact: Every part of the plant contains colchicine, a toxic alkaloid used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular subtropical tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers just as the leaves emerge. In the Southern Hemisphere, late October is the peak of its bloom, carpeting streets with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia (Brisbane, Sydney, Grafton), South Africa (Pretoria), and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, whose bloom signals the start of the exam season for many students.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that is one of the earliest camellias to bloom, producing fragrant, delicate single or semi-double flowers with prominent golden stamens. It attracts bees and other pollinators in late autumn when little else is blooming.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, the UK, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.
